name: Granite Axle
specific_features: Automated beacon (distress, navigation, or unknown purpose)
description: Granite Axle is a medium-sized rocky world whose most prominent feature is a colossal mountain range that circles the entire equator like an axle through the planet's center. This equatorial ridge rises to over twenty kilometers in places, its granite faces carved by wind into jagged spires and deep notches. On either side, barren plains of gray and brown stone stretch to the poles, broken only by ancient impact craters and dry canyons where wind-driven dust streams like ghostly rivers.

The thin atmosphere carries sound poorly, creating an oppressive silence broken only by the whistle of wind through the equatorial mountains. Temperature swings are dramatic, the thin air unable to retain heat, and mornings on the sunlit side bring a brief, intense warmth that gives way to bone-deep cold within hours of sunset. The sky is a deep purple even at midday, and stars remain visible near the horizon at all times, lending the world a perpetual twilight quality.

The equatorial ridge has served as a navigation landmark for centuries, and an automated beacon of uncertain origin sits atop its highest peak, broadcasting a carrier signal that predates human settlement in the sector. Smugglers have long used the canyon systems as cache points, the thin atmosphere and low traffic making detection difficult. Microbial colonies survive in sheltered crevices along the ridge where mineral-rich groundwater seeps to the surface, their metabolism so slow they were initially mistaken for mineral deposits.

Granite Axle's strategic value lies in its position along several major trade routes and its abundant mineral resources, though its harsh conditions have discouraged permanent settlement. The smuggler caches in the canyons are an open secret that law enforcement has been unable to eliminate due to the sheer volume of hiding places. The beacon continues to broadcast without apparent power source, and its signal has recently been detected modulating in response to ship traffic, suggesting it may be more than a simple navigational aid.
